speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, I need to check for signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome; have you experienced any muscle rigidity, tremors, or excessive sweating recently? speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your symptoms of fever, altered mentation, profuse sweating, and generalized rigidity in the context of haloperidol use are highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I need to confirm this by checking your laboratory values, so REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase.

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated Creatine Kinase level confirms rhabdomyolysis, which, combined with your fever, generalized rigidity, and altered mentation while on haloperidol, is diagnostic of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
